rationale: Mid-market engineering teams are accumulating $300–$500/developer/month in AI tooling subscriptions (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT Team, Claude Pro, etc.) with no consolidated view of utilization or ROI — a pain corroborated by multiple HN threads, Reddit discussions, and the emergence of at least two funded competitors (Zylo, Torii) in adjacent SaaS management. Willingness-to-pay is evidenced by competitor pricing ($15k–$50k/year enterprise contracts for SaaS management platforms) and job postings for 'AI tooling procurement' roles, though no direct 'I'd pay $X for this specific tool' quote was found. The pain clears the 5-distinct-evidence threshold and has at least one clear WTP signal (competitor pricing), but the responsiveness signal remains untested.
